why: A tasks.json is confirmed by its text only when that text carries an indicator; one that just runs something on folder open is review. A published campaign file is confirmed by what it is: a tasks.json whose SHA-256 is in hashes.txt is that file whatever it says. The fixture runs a command that is in no indicator list, so only its hash can confirm it, and a neighbour one byte different stays review. (The tasks.json OpenSourceMalware published also carries a strong.txt string today; its hash is a second, independent reason.) The runner adds the fixture's hash to a copy of ioc/ (ADR-0045).

findings.match: tasks.json matches a known campaign file (corpus fixture: tasks.json)
